title: Learnable Prompt as Pseudo-Imputation: Rethinking the Necessity of Traditional EHR Data Imputation in Downstream Clinical Prediction

problem.claim: Extensive missing values in electronic health records make it difficult for deep neural networks to model patient health status directly.

gap.claim: Existing impute-then-regress and jointly optimized imputation protocols require additional imputation models and can introduce non-real data, optimization complexity, demanding data requirements, power loss, and biased estimation.

contributions.claim: The work proposes Learnable Prompt as Pseudo-Imputation as a training protocol for EHR analysis that constructs a learnable prompt to model downstream models' implicit preferences for missing values without introducing imputed data.
PAI is described as a plug-and-play protocol that can be integrated into existing and future EHR analysis models.
The code is publicly deployed to support reproduction of the reported results and EHR analysis tasks.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report significant performance improvement for state-of-the-art EHR analysis models on four real-world datasets across two clinical prediction tasks.
The authors report higher robustness under data insufficiency and high missing rates.

narrative_sequence.summary: EHR-based patient health-status analysis is a fundamental medical-informatics problem.
Extensive EHR missingness challenges direct DNN modeling, while existing imputation protocols introduce additional modeling requirements and limitations.
The authors propose PAI, which uses a learnable prompt as pseudo-imputation instead of generating imputed data.
The authors report improved performance across datasets and tasks, along with greater robustness under insufficient data and high missingness.
PAI is presented as broadly integrable, with publicly available code.

source_observation.claim: The proposed protocol models a downstream model's implicit preferences for missing values through a learnable prompt rather than constructing imputed data.

interpretation.claim: When preprocessing can inject potentially unrealistic values, directly learning task-relevant missing-value behavior may be an alternative.

application.claim: Consider task-integrated representations of missingness for prediction settings where conventional imputation may distort downstream estimation.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this approach is preferable outside the reported EHR tasks, datasets, or missingness conditions.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the four datasets, two clinical prediction tasks, baseline configurations, or quantitative performance results.
The abstract does not describe the learnable prompt architecture, training procedure, or optimization details.
The abstract does not independently verify the reported robustness, performance improvements, or reproducibility.
